result.title: BDNet: Fast-slow thinking is all you need
result.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures, this manuscript is an early draft
result.summary: We present BDNet, a hierarchical image-classification backbone built around fast image features and slow statistical references. Its baseline deformation operator (BDO) transforms the deviation of a feature from a stage-specific reference through a low-rank projection and a learned channel scale. Rather than computing pairwise token similarity, the branch operates directly on baseline-relative residuals with complexity linear in the token count. Each of four reference buffers accumulates detached stage statistics during training and remains frozen at inference. A four-stage pyramid with depths $(2,2,6,2)$ and widths $(96,192,384,768)$ yields a 20.70M-parameter classifier at $224\times224$ resolution. We organize an ImageNet-1K study around clean classification, eight controlled ablations, and Gaussian-noise, contrast, and brightness perturbations. The central hypothesis is that a slow reference can improve the robustness of a compact representation while retaining a simple tensor implementation. We distinguish this training-time statistical mechanism from input-dependent attention and make its linear inference behavior explicit.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BDNet，一个图像分类骨干：以基线变形算子把特征相对阶段性参考的偏差经低秩投影与通道缩放处理，四个参考缓冲区在训练中累积统计量、推理时冻结，并在 ImageNet-1K 上考察干净精度、消融与噪声、对比度、亮度扰动。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「慢」参考仅为训练期统计量、明确区别于输入相关注意力，与 LVR 主线关联较弱；但以参考相对残差替代成对 token 相似度、复杂度随 token 数线性增长，可能为 latent 状态中相似度/注意力结构及缓存式参考的设计提供核查线索。
